test_shot.purpose: Prove identity continuity and transformation quality before producing the remaining trailer
test_shot.prompt: Create an eight-second 16:9 stylized 3D cinematic transition for Beat My Track, anchored to the supplied actual compact-car reference. Preserve its boxy three-door hatchback silhouette, two round headlights total, horizontal rectangular grille, wheelbase and original unbranded identity throughout. Use one stable high-oblique overhead tracking composition with no visible horizon and a readable car. The compact travels briskly through a single continuous sweeping road bend. Seconds 0-2.5: green forest, asphalt, navy blue and warm-white twin-stripe livery. A physically motivated fine sand curtain crosses the lens: seconds 2.5-5: the identical corner becomes golden desert while the car changes to red/cream rally livery with the actual referenced rally kit. A soft white snow-spray wipe crosses the lens: seconds 5-8: the same driving direction and car pose continue through winter scenery, the compact now yellow/navy with the actual referenced wide-arch kit and rear aero. The car stays visible, complete and rigid; changes resolve at the wipe rather than melting geometry. Convey speed through modest environmental motion blur, wheel rotation and small material-appropriate dust or snow spray. Mature game-like stylized 3D, controlled natural colours and directional light. No photoreal live-action substitution, oversized toy car, real-world branding, UI, captions, floating parts, extra wheels, random camera cut, teleportation or traffic. End with a clean readable winter corner suitable for a cut into real gameplay. Engine, tire and environmental sound only; no voice-over or music.
